_comment_globals: The WHATWG global attributes. A bare entry is a free string; an entry with a `type` is
typed (`bool` / `int` / `float` / `string`, or a token list for an enum).
`row` is the second axis, independent of `type`. It defaults to `"closed"`, which emits
`Attr { c | <name> : Supported } msg` and puts the name in every element's closed `Attrs`
alias. `"open"` emits `Attr c msg` and puts it in NO element's alias, so the setter
composes onto anything structurally.
Five entries are open: `dir`, `lang`, `tabindex`, `hidden`, `title`. The test is whether
an attribute's VALIDITY depends on the element, which is the same line `TypedHtml.Aria`
already draws between `label : String -> Attr c msg` (open — a label is never invalid)
and `role : Value tags -> Attr { c | role : tags } msg` (closed — `role="tab"` on a bare
<div> should be rejected). These five have `label`'s shape: no element restricts what
value they may carry, so a closed row on them only ever rejects a correct call.
Opening them HERE is what makes them work everywhere. An open setter needs no row
membership to compose, so every brand elm-cem generates (elm-m3e, elm-calcite,
elm-shoelace, elm-fluent-ui, elm-web-awesome) picks these up by ordinary structural
unification, with no config edit of its own and no duplicate per-brand `Dir` type. The
motivating case: elm-m3e's docs could not put `dir` on `m3e-theme`, because m3e's config
never populated `_globals` and inherited elm-cem's four-item default, so `M3e.Theme.Attrs`
had no `dir` field — an absence nobody ever decided on.
Deliberately still CLOSED: `class`/`id`/`slot`/`style` (already reach every element that
needs them, and `class`/`style` carry bespoke merging companions — a separate cleanup),
and `popover`/`contenteditable`/`is` plus the text-editing hints (`autocapitalize`,
`autocorrect`, `enterkeyhint`, `inputmode`, `writingsuggestions`), which interact with a
component's own behaviour (top-layer stacking, rich editing) in ways the i18n/a11y core
does not. Those deserve individual review, not a blanket include.
Every one of these used to be a bare string, which INVERTED four of them: `hidden "false"`
HID the element and `inert "false"` made it inert, because these are boolean CONTENT
attributes — any value at all (except `hidden="until-found"`) is the true state.
Which shape each one gets, and why it is not the other shape:
- bool  — `autofocus` / `inert` / `itemscope` are pure presence booleans.
- enum  — `hidden` is NOT a bool: `hidden="until-found"` keeps the element findable by
find-in-page and is what reveals it, so the value is load-bearing.
`draggable` / `contenteditable` / `spellcheck` / `writingsuggestions` are NOT
bools either: their literal "false" is a real, distinct state — absence means
`auto` / inherit-from-ancestor, `"false"` means explicitly off.
- int   — `tabindex` must admit NEGATIVE values (`-1` = focusable by script only,
not by sequential navigation), so it cannot be a natural or a string.
- string — free text (`accesskey`, `id`, `lang`, `title`, the microdata `item*` set,
`nonce`, `slot`, `is`) plus `class`/`style`, which have bespoke merging
setters (`classList` / `style p v` / `styleList`) in the emitter.
`is` STAYS in this roster and gets NO setter, and the two facts are not in conflict.
This roster is a description of HTML, where `is` is a global attribute; the generator
then omits it, because elm/virtual-dom cannot write it. Customized built-in elements
are opted in only at CREATION time — `document.createElement(tag, { is })` — and
`_VirtualDom_render` creates every node with `_VirtualDom_doc.createElement(vNode.__tag)`,
no options argument. By the time virtual-dom applies any attribute fact the element
already exists as its plain built-in self, so `setAttribute("is", …)` cannot upgrade it;
and there is no `is` IDL attribute, so a property write is an inert expando either.
Do NOT delete the entry to 'match' the emitted surface. Removing it would make the
curation drift below the spec, which `scripts/check-whatwg.mjs` gate 1 exists to catch,
and would erase the record of a decided fact. The gate's KERNEL_BLOCKED table holds the
reason and asserts the omission actually happened; see `Attr.kernelBlockedReason` in
elm-cem for every blocked name and the kernel source behind it.
_comment_controlled: The CONTROLLED attributes: those whose LIVE state is a DOM property, and whose content
attribute only ever sets the DEFAULT/initial state. Each gets TWO setters — the plain name
writes the property, `default<Name>` writes the content attribute — mirroring HTML's own IDL
split (`value`/`defaultValue`, `checked`/`defaultChecked`, `selected`/`defaultSelected`,
`muted`/`defaultMuted`). The companion shares the base capability row, so no element's
`Attrs` record grows a field.
Every entry carries an `elements` SCOPE, and that is not optional bookkeeping — the roster
used to be keyed by attribute NAME alone, which is a claim about `HTMLElement`, and `value`
is not one attribute. Seven elements declare a `value` content attribute in
manifest/native.cem.json (button, data, input, li, meter, option, progress) at THREE
different IDL types: `DOMString` on button/data/option, `long` on li, and `double` on
meter/progress. `Ir.property "value" (Json.Encode.string "abc")` against a `double` is a
Web IDL TypeError — thrown inside `_VirtualDom_applyFacts`, i.e. mid-patch, where it takes
down the whole Elm render loop rather than one node. `TypedHtml.Text.value "abc"` on a
<progress> was that crash. Measured in a real app: the exception escapes the
animation-frame draw callback, Elm re-schedules the frame, and it re-throws about 60 times
a second, forever, on a page that is otherwise idle — a frozen DOM with no Elm crash
screen and no error in the model.
Scoping is HALF the fix, and on its own it is the wrong half. It makes each element's OWN
module correct — `TypedHtml.Input.value` live, `TypedHtml.Text.value` a content attribute
— but `TypedHtml.Attributes` is the LOOSE surface, one open producer admitted by every
element whose row carries the field. So the question `elements` cannot answer is which
form THAT setter takes, and the answer is the PROPERTY form (elm-cem
`Model.sharedAttrs` breaks the tie there, deliberately): `TypedHtml.Attributes.value
model.text` on a text input is the single most-used call in the library, and the content
attribute silently pins it once the input is dirty (issue #41). Publishing the attribute
form here traded a rare crash for common silent staleness on the hottest path.
Which leaves the crash to be made UNREPRESENTABLE instead of merely avoided. That is a
capability-ROW job, not a form job — see `_comment_renames` below. <progress>, <meter> and
<li> leave the `value` row entirely, so `TypedHtml.Attributes.value` applied to one of them
does not compile. The three elements that KEEP the row (button, data, option) all have a
reflected `DOMString value`, so the shared property write is not merely survivable there,
it reaches the content attribute anyway.
Why each entry is scoped the way it is (each verified against manifest/native.cem.json):
- value    — declared by 7 elements; only <input> has a live value that DIVERGES from the
content attribute (the dirty-value flag), which is issue #41 / NB2c. Of the
other six, three reflect and stay on the row; three have a numeric IDL type
and leave it.
- checked  — declared by <input> only, so the scope is documentation rather than a change.
Stated anyway: the name-only form is what let `value` go wrong, and an entry
that looks global invites the next element to be swept in silently.
- selected — declared by <option> only. The `selected` content attribute is
`defaultSelected`; the live selection is the IDL property.
- muted    — declared by <audio> and <video>, both of which need it. This is the BUG the
roster was originally extended for: the `muted` content attribute sets only
`defaultMuted`, so `Ir.attribute "muted" ""` is inert after first render and
`muted True` never muted a playing <video>.
Consequences of the split form, stated so they are not a surprise:
- `TypedHtml.Attributes.value` writes the DOM property, and `TypedHtml.Attributes.
defaultValue` is its serializing companion (the content attribute — what SSR and
`outerHTML` show, and what a form reset restores to). Both claim `value : Supported`,
so no `Attrs` row grows a field.
- button, data and option keep a LOCAL content-attribute `value` in their own home
modules (`TypedHtml.Button.value`, `TypedHtml.Text.value`, `TypedHtml.Select.value`),
because that is the form those elements actually want and delegating to the shared
property setter would quietly stop serializing. Their generated docs name
`TypedHtml.Input.value` as the live one.
`resyncs: false` is not a preference — it is a fact about elm/virtual-dom. Its controlled-input
machinery is hardcoded to two NAMES: `_VirtualDom_diffFacts` re-emits an unchanged fact, and
`_VirtualDom_applyFacts` writes-when-the-DOM-differs, only for `value` and `checked`. PROP facts
are organized as raw JS values, so for any other name `true === true` skips the write forever.
The property form therefore fixes INERTNESS but not RESYNC for `selected`/`muted`, and the
generated docs must say so and name the event to listen to.
Not listed, and why: `<textarea>`'s default value is its CHILD TEXT (there is no `value` content
attribute on textarea) and `<output>`'s `defaultValue` is a property with no backing content
attribute at all. Neither declares a `value` attribute in manifest/native.cem.json, so neither
earns a companion here. Were one added, add that element to `value`'s `elements` scope and mark
it `"propertyOnly": ["value"]` — the generator then emits the property setter and suppresses
the dishonest `default*` one. (`propertyOnly` outside the scope is rejected: there is no live
property there to keep.)
_comment_variants: Ergonomic ALTERNATIVE setters for attributes whose spec-correct type is a string.
This follows HTML's own convention rather than inventing one: `HTMLInputElement` has
`value`, `valueAsNumber` and `valueAsDate`. The BASE setter keeps the type the spec
demands and the variant sits beside it, claiming the SAME capability row — so no
element's `Attrs` record grows a field and an element that admits `step` admits every
way of writing it.
Why each base must stay a String, and why the variant cannot replace it:
- step   — `step="any"` is a legal keyword that disables step-matching. No `Float`
expresses it, so `step` is a String and `stepAsNumber` is the convenience.
- coords — `coords="0,0,82,126"` is a COMMA-SEPARATED LIST. No single number is ever
a valid value; it was typed `number` (a native-manifest-gen mis-read of the
WHATWG cell 'Valid list of floating-point numbers'), which made every
<area> unaddressable. `coordsAsInts` comma-joins a `List Int`.
- value  — a String submission value on button, data, input and option. This is HTML's
own `HTMLInputElement.value` / `valueAsNumber` pair, and it exists for the
numeric-typed <input>s (`type="number"`, `type="range"`). A variant always
writes the SAME fact as its base, so it follows `value`'s per-element form
(see `_comment_controlled`): where `value` is the live property (<input>, and
the shared `TypedHtml.Attributes`) `valueAsNumber` renders through
`String.fromFloat` and then `Json.Encode.string`, so it writes the same JS
TYPE as `value` — a property fact alternating between number and string
would defeat virtual-dom's identity diff and its `value`/`checked` resync
special-case. Where `value` is a content attribute (button, data, option)
there is no JS value to keep consistent and `valueAsNumber` is a plain
`Ir.attribute` write.
`base` names a SETTER, not a DOM attribute, and that is why <progress>, <meter> and <li>
get no `valueAsNumber`: `_comment_renames` moves their `value` to a different setter name,
so they are no longer part of the `value` vocabulary. Nothing is lost — their renamed
setters are ALREADY numeric (Float and Int respectively), so a Float variant beside them
would be a second name for one fact, and on <li> a wrong one (an ordinal is an integer).
NOT here, deliberately: a `valueAsDate` / Posix variant. HTML's `valueAsDate` takes a
JS `Date` OBJECT, and `Json.Encode` cannot construct one — the setter would be
unreachable from Elm at any type. Format the string in Elm instead.
_comment_renames: The `value` attribute is FOUR different value spaces wearing one HTML name, and the phantom
capability row is where that has to be admitted. A row is a claim about which elements ADMIT
a setter, so two elements sharing the `value` row are asserting that one body is right for
both. For <input> and <progress> that assertion is false in the strongest possible way:
`TypedHtml.Attributes.value` writes the DOM property (see `_comment_controlled` for why it
must), `HTMLProgressElement.value` is a restricted IDL `double`, and Web IDL answers
`progress.value = "abc"` with a TypeError thrown mid-patch — which kills the Elm render
loop, not one node.
So the three elements whose `value` is NUMERIC leave the row. `_renames` moves an
attribute's setter name, and elm-cem moves the capability row with it (`elmName` and
`capName` together), so a renamed attribute is a genuinely different capability:
<progress>/<meter>/<li> `Attrs` records have no `value` field at all, and
`TypedHtml.Attributes.value` applied to one is a COMPILE error. That is the difference
between avoiding the crash and making it unrepresentable, and only the second one survives
the next refactor.
Why the NAME has to diverge and not just the row: <data>, <meter> and <progress> all live in
the `Text` home module, and <data>'s value is a reflected DOMString. One Elm module cannot
expose one name at two types — elm-cem's `guardHomeAttrTypes` refuses the run rather than
silently publishing one of them (that guard exists because the `datetime` regression did
exactly that). A distinct name resolves it: `TypedHtml.Text` exposes `value : String` for
<data> AND `valueNumeric : Float` for <meter>/<progress>.
The names, and why not others:
- valueNumeric : Float — <meter> and <progress>. `HTMLMeterElement.value` and
`HTMLProgressElement.value` are both `attribute double value`, and there is no keyword
in either value space that a Float cannot express, so unlike `step` the numeric type is
the whole story rather than a variant of a String one.
- valueOrdinal : Int — <li>. `HTMLLIElement.value` is `attribute long value`: the list
item's ordinal position. Int, not Float, because "item 3.5" is not a thing; the manifest
description already calls it an ordinal. It gets its own name rather than sharing
`valueNumeric` because <li> is in the `Grouping` home and <meter>/<progress> are in
`Text` — sharing the name would put an Int and a Float on ONE shared capability row, and
elm-cem would then publish one of the two types on `TypedHtml.Attributes` and leave the
other as a local setter. That is the `datetime` shape again, just below the guard's
threshold. Two names, two rows, no choice to get wrong.
- NOT `valueAsFloat`/`valueAsInt`: the `As<Type>` suffix is this config's `_variants`
convention, and a variant SHARES its base's capability row (`stepAsNumber` claims
`step`). These do the opposite — they exist to leave the row — so borrowing that suffix
would signal precisely the wrong thing.
- NOT `valueFloat`/`valueInt`: that is the spelling of the abandoned suffix-the-loser
scheme elm-cem's `Generate.SharedAttrs` documents as dead code and a decoy. Reusing it
invites the reader to look for a mechanism that does not exist.
`attrTypes` below is the other half and is not optional. Without it the renamed setters are
still `String -> Attr`, which is the same lie under a new name: the manifest types all seven
`value` attributes as `string` (correct for a CONTENT attribute, which is always a string),
so the numeric IDL type has to come from config. With it, `<progress>` takes a Float and
`String.fromFloat` guarantees the serialized attribute is a valid floating-point number —
the non-finite string that started all this is now unconstructible.

Li._comment_attrTypes: `HTMLLIElement.value` is `attribute long value` — the ordinal position of the item. See `_comment_renames`: renamed to `valueOrdinal` so it leaves the shared `value` capability row, and typed `int` so the setter matches the value space rather than accepting any string and silently coercing to 0 through ToInt32.

Meter._comment_attrTypes: `HTMLMeterElement.value` is `attribute double value`, a RESTRICTED double: Web IDL rejects a non-finite value with a TypeError. See `_comment_renames` — renamed to `valueNumeric` so it leaves the shared `value` row, and typed `float` so `String.fromFloat` is the only way to produce the attribute string.

Progress._comment_attrTypes: `HTMLProgressElement.value` is `attribute double value`, a RESTRICTED double. `progress.value = "abc"` and `progress.value = "1e999"` are both TypeErrors — verified in a browser — and thrown mid-patch they spin the Elm render loop at ~60 exceptions/second indefinitely. See `_comment_renames`: renamed to `valueNumeric` so it leaves the shared `value` row, and typed `float` so the non-finite string is unconstructible.
